It is used as a bulk sweetener in foods and as a sweetener or excipient in pharmaceuticals. Xylitol is also used as a sweetening agent in sugar-free preparations as it is non- cariogenic and is less likely to cause dental caries than sucrose. It is under investigation for the prevention of dental caries and acute otitis media. It was formerly considered as a substitute for glucose in intravenous nutrition but such use has generally been abandoned due to adverse effects. Dental caries. Chewing-gum containing xylitol appears to have a useful role in the prevention of dental caries (p.180).1-5 1. Edgar WM. Sugar substitutes, chewing gum and dental caries— a review. However, a randomised study4 found xylitol to be ineffective when given only during an acute respiratory- tract infection. 1. Uhari M, et al.
